_comment: Error taxonomy for the Clinical Note Hallucination Guard. Categories are adapted from documented failure modes in the ambient-scribe / clinical-documentation-quality literature (fabrication, distortion, omission, misattribution), plus two clinically-motivated subtypes (numeric/medication error, negation error) that are called out separately because they carry outsized clinical risk relative to how small the text change is.

categories.name: Fabrication
categories.definition: A finding, symptom, or detail stated in the note that does not appear anywhere in the source transcript, in any form.
categories.example: Note says 'patient reports nausea' but nausea was never mentioned in the conversation.

categories.name: Distortion
categories.definition: A detail that IS present in the transcript but has been altered in the note — e.g. the right symptom with the wrong severity, duration, or qualifier.
categories.example: Patient said pain started '2 days ago'; note says 'started 2 weeks ago'.

categories.name: Numeric / Medication Error
categories.definition: A specific number (dose, vital sign, lab value, frequency) or a medication name is wrong in the note relative to the transcript. Checked deterministically wherever possible, not just by LLM judgment, because these are exact-checkable and carry the highest clinical risk of any category.

categories.name: Negation Error
categories.definition: A denial is flipped into an affirmation, or vice versa. Small textual change, potentially large clinical consequence.
categories.example: Patient said 'I don't have any chest pain'; note says 'patient reports chest pain'.

categories.name: Misattribution
categories.definition: A real detail from the transcript is attached to the wrong source or subject — e.g. family history recorded as the patient's own history, or a detail about one symptom attached to a different body system.
categories.example: Patient said 'my father has diabetes'; note says 'patient has a history of diabetes'.

categories.name: Omission
categories.definition: A clinically relevant detail was stated in the transcript but is entirely missing from the note. Tracked as a secondary metric — the guard's primary job is catching invented/altered content (errors of commission), but omission recall is reported separately since it is a different failure mode with a different detection approach.
categories.example: Patient mentioned a known penicillin allergy; note does not mention allergies at all.
